segments.say: Now that your body is soft and heavy, let's spend a few quiet minutes with a kind thought. Earlier tonight, we saw that people aren't exactly the same in every room. We shift a little, depending on where we are and who we're with. So let's visit a few of those versions of you now, slowly, and say something gentle to each one.

You don't need to pick which version is the real you. That's the lovely thing. They're all real. The careful one and the playful one. The quiet one and the chatty one. Each one appears when its moment comes, the way different birds sing at different times of day. None of them is pretending. All of them belong to you.

Let's start with the version of you who works, or studies, or looks after things during the day. Picture that version now, a little focused, a little busy, perhaps a bit more serious than you are at home. That version has tried hard today. Maybe it got things right. Maybe it got some things wrong. Either way, it showed up, and that counts.

If you like, say something kind to that working version of you, quietly, in your own head. Something like, thank you for today. You did your best with what you had. You can put it all down now. Let that busy, careful version of you take off its shoes, sit down somewhere soft, and finally stop for the night, at last.

Now picture the version of you that appears with friends, or with the people you feel easiest around. Maybe that version laughs more. Maybe it tells longer stories, or sits more comfortably in silence. It might be louder than the working you, or softer. Either way, it's a version that feels at home, and other people are glad of it.

Remember that the people who love you often see parts of you that you overlook. Your warmth, perhaps. Your patience, or your humour, or the way you notice when someone's quiet. They're holding those pieces of you right now, somewhere, in their own memories. Let that be a comforting thought. You're known, a little, in many places at once, and that's a gift.

And there's another version, too, the one that sometimes feels awkward. The one that said the wrong thing, or went quiet when it wanted to speak, or felt out of place in a busy room. That version deserves kindness most of all. It was doing its best in a moment that felt hard. Let it rest now. It's welcome here, too.

And now, the version of you that's here right now, alone at night. Lying in the dark, listening, resting. This might be the quietest version of you, the one nobody else sees. It doesn't need to perform, or explain, or be clever. It doesn't need to be a type. It can simply be tired, and warm, and drifting slowly towards sleep.

And somewhere in this quiet night, our imagined Nora is asleep now. The laptop is closed on the bedside table. The quiz tab is gone, and so is the little rare type it promised her. The room is dark, and still, and cool. Moonlight rests softly on the curtains. She's breathing slowly and deeply, just the way you are now.

Picture her resting there, no longer wondering which kind of person she is. She doesn't need an answer tonight. In the morning, she'll be the careful Nora at work, the laughing Nora with friends, and the quiet Nora at the end of the day. All of them her. None of them a box. And for now, simply asleep, warm and still.

You did enough today. You belong, just as you are. You can rest now. And you are still growing, slowly and quietly, the way all people do. Four small sentences, for every version of you. You can say them silently, or simply let them float by. Either way, they're yours to keep, tonight and for as long as you like.

Now imagine all of those versions of you gathering in one warm room, around a small fire. The working you, the friendly you, the awkward you, the quiet you. They sit together comfortably, like old friends at the end of a long trip. Nobody is in charge. Nobody is being compared. They're just sharing the warmth, and growing quietly sleepy together.

They're not strangers to each other. They're one person, moving gently through many rooms. That's what we saw tonight, really. Personality isn't a single fixed picture. It's more like a familiar pattern, a way of being that changes its shape a little in each room, but always carries the same warmth underneath. Like one song, played softly in many different keys.

So be gentle with yourself, tomorrow, and the day after, and the day after that. On the days you feel bold, and the days you feel shy. On the days you're organised, and the days you lose your keys. On the days you recognise yourself, and the days you surprise yourself. All of those days belong to the same kind, changing, ordinary, lovely person.

Every version of you is welcome here. The one who tried hard, the one who laughed, the one who stumbled, and the one who's lying in the dark right now, drifting slowly towards sleep. None of them need to wait outside. None of them need to earn their place. They can all come in, sit down by the fire, and rest.

show.text: Every version of you is welcome here.

segments.say: Let your breathing slow down a little more now, as if all those versions of you were breathing together, in one slow rhythm. In, softly. And out, even more softly. Each breath gathering them closer, warming them, settling them down. There's no hurry. The fire is low and warm, and the night is still young, and there's plenty of time.

If any thoughts come up now, about who you are or who you should be, let them pass by like slow clouds over a dark sky. You don't need to solve them tonight. Those are questions for a bright morning, with a cup of something warm. For now, the only thing to do is rest, and let the night be kind.

Perhaps there's soft rain on a roof somewhere above you now. Not a storm. Just a steady, gentle patter, the kind of rain that makes being indoors feel safe. Each drop small and unhurried. Each one landing, and then gone. Let the sound of it wash over all the versions of you, and carry the last of the day away.

Let yourself drift a little further down now. The room is dark. The blanket is warm. Your body is heavy and soft. And all the versions of you are curled up together, quiet and content, around the last glow of the fire. There's nothing left to do tonight. Nothing to answer. Nothing to become. Just this slow, easy breath, in and out.

In a little while, we'll come to the very end of our evening, with a last look back and a quiet goodnight. There's no need to stay awake for it. If you're already drifting, keep drifting. That's the very best thing you could do. And if you're still listening, just keep resting, softly, here, with me, in the warm dark.
